title: Your user persona is quietly lying to you
description:
A persona is a composite sketch of a user type built from real research — useful shared shorthand for "who are we building for." But it only ever answers who, never why. This Short shows how interviews, Jobs-to-be-Done, and personas actually fit together, and why teams over-rely on the persona.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/02-understanding-customers-users/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Your user persona is quietly lying to you. Not on purpose. It's just built to answer the wrong question.
A persona is a composite sketch of a user type, built from real research. It keeps the team aligned on who we're building for. Handy shorthand: would Erin actually use this button?
Here's the catch. A persona describes who. It never tells you why. Why someone hires your product, the progress they want, that's Jobs-to-be-Done.
Think of it as a pipeline. Interviews are the raw method. Jobs-to-be-Done is the lens you listen with. The persona is just the artifact you write down afterward.
So keep the list short. Two to four, revisited whenever new research contradicts them. And never let a persona replace asking why.
